History:
Initially,
the Emperor heard that in the Western Regions there was a deity
named "Buddha."
He sent an envoy to Tiānzhú
to seek its doctrine,
obtaining its scriptures and bringing back a shramana.
Its scriptures excelled in grand and magnificent words.
Those proficient in its path
were called shramana.
From "Tōngjiàn: Records of Emperor Hàn Míng."
The Zhào ruler Shí Lè,
because the Tiānzhú monk Fótúchéng predicted successes and failures
with frequent accuracy,
revered and served him.
When Shí Hǔ ascended the throne,
he honored him even more diligently,
clothing him in silk brocade,
and having him ride in a carved carriage.
On court assembly days,
the crown prince and nobles
would support him up the palace steps.
The master of ceremonies would call out "Great Monk,"
and all seated would rise.
He had the Minister of Works Lǐ Nóng inquire about his well-being morning and evening,
while the crown prince and nobles
paid respects every five days.
The people, influenced by this,
largely turned to Buddhism.
Wherever Chéng was,
none dared to spit or shed tears in his direction.
They competed to build temples
and shaved their heads to become monks.
From "Tōngjiàn: Records of Jìn Chéng."
The Qín king Yáo Xīng,
taking Jiūmóluóshí as the National Teacher,
revered him as a deity.
He personally led his officials and shramanas
to listen to Jiūmóluóshí expound over three hundred volumes of Buddhist scriptures.
They constructed large monasteries and stūpas,
and shramanas engaged in meditation
often numbered in the thousands.
Officials and nobles down to the lowest ranks all revered the Buddha.
Thus, the provinces and commanderies were transformed,
with nine out of ten households following Buddhism.
From "Records of Jìn'ān."
The Emperor, because the monk Huìlín was skilled in discourse,
discussed major court affairs with him,
and thus he came to participate in authority and important matters.
Guests gathered like spokes to a hub,
and the carriages at his gate often numbered several tens.
Gifts and bribes from all directions came in succession,
with seven or eight feasts laid out
and seats always filled.
Lín wore tall clogs
and draped in sable furs,
appointed messengers and secretaries.
Kuàijī's Kǒng Jì once visited him,
encountering the crowd of guests,
and could only exchange pleasantries.
Jì sighed, saying,
"So there is a black-robed prime minister;
one could say caps and shoes have lost their proper places!"
From "Tōngjiàn: Records of Sòng Gāozǔ of Southern History."
At that time, Buddhism flourished in Luòyáng,

Huáng Chūpíng,
a man from Dānxī.
At age fifteen,
his family sent him to herd sheep.
A Daoist priest, seeing his goodness and diligence,
took him to a stone chamber on Jīnhuá Mountain.
After over forty years,
he no longer missed home.
His elder brother Chūqǐ searched for him
but could not find him.
Later, in the market, there was a priest skilled in divination,
so he went to consult him.
The priest said: "In Jīnhuá Mountain, there is a shepherd boy.
Is he your brother,
or not?"
Chūqǐ followed the priest to seek him.
Seeing his brother,
he was both sad and joyful.
He asked where the sheep were.
Chūpíng said: "They are nearby, east of the mountain."
Chūqǐ went to look,
but saw no sheep,
only countless white stones.
Returning, he said:
"There are no sheep."
Chūpíng said: "The sheep are there,
but you, brother, cannot see them."
Then they went together.
Chūpíng shouted, "Sheep, rise!"
What were white stones
all rose and became sheep,
tens of thousands of them.
Chūqǐ said: "My brother has such divine powers,
can I learn them?"
Chūpíng said: "Only by loving the Way can one attain it."
Chūqǐ then abandoned his wife and children,
stayed with Chūpíng,
and together they consumed pine resin and poria for a thousand days.
They could sit and vanish instantly,
and cast no shadow at noon.
There was a village of youths,
later they returned to their hometown.
Most of their relatives had died,
so they left again.
Teaching his arts to Nánbó Féng,

Chūqǐ changed his name to Lǔ Bān,
and Chūpíng to Chìsōngzǐ.

Ten Continents with Preface
Preface states: "Emperor Wǔ of Hàn, having heard from the Queen Mother about the vast seas in all directions,
Learned of ten continents: Zǔzhōu, Yíngzhōu, Xuánzhōu, Yánzhōu, Chángzhōu, Yuánzhōu, Liúzhōu, Shēngzhōu, Fènglínzhōu, and Jùkūzhōu,
All places rarely reached by human traces.
Also knowing Dōngfāng Shuò was no ordinary mortal,
He invited him to a secluded chamber,
And personally inquired about the locations of the ten continents.
The names of exotic things
Were thus recorded in writing.
Fāng Shuò said: 'I once followed my master's footsteps:
North to Zhūlíng's Fúsāng gateway,
Sù Sea's Míngyè hills,
Chúnyáng's ridges,
Below Shǐqīng,
Between moon palaces,
Traveling internally through seven hills,
Circling centrally through ten continents;
Treading on Chìxiàn while roaming five sacred mountains,
Crossing marshes while resting at famous peaks.
From youth till now,
I've wandered through six heavens,
Traversed the eight extremes thus.
Not like those who ascend to numinous realms,
Attendants hearing truth,
Ascending and descending nine heavens,
Piercingly viewing all directions;
North reaching Hooked Array alongside Canopy,
South soaring to Tàidān while resting in Huǒxià;
East reaching Tōngyáng's rosy clouds,
West approaching Hánkōng's wilds;
Where sun and moon don't reach,
Where Milky Way doesn't accompany;
Above, no further substance,
Below, no further base.
What I know is thus,
Ashamed it's insufficient to match such vastness.'"
Zǔzhōu
Zǔzhōu is located nearby in the Eastern Sea,
spanning five hundred lǐ in area,
seventy thousand lǐ from the western shore.
Upon it grows the herb of immortality,
shaped like wild rice sprouts,
three to four chǐ long.
If the dead are covered with this herb,
they immediately come back to life.
If ingested,
it grants eternal life.
In the past, many wrongful deaths occurred in Qín Shǐhuáng's gardens;
along the paths, there were birds,
resembling crows,
that carried this herb to cover the faces of the dead,
who would then rise and revive on their own.
Officials reported this,
and Shǐhuáng sent an envoy with the herb to consult Guǐgǔ Xiānshēng of the northern outskirts.
Guǐgǔ Xiānshēng said: "I have heard that on Zǔzhōu in the Eastern Sea, there is an herb of immortality,
growing in jade fields,
sometimes called the Spirit-Nourishing Mushroom,
its leaves resembling wild rice sprouts,
growing in clusters,
one plant can revive one person."
Shǐhuáng then sighed and said: "Can it be gathered?"
So he sent Xú Fú with three hundred boys and three hundred girls,
leading a fleet of tower ships to sea in search of Zǔzhōu,
and they never returned.
Fú,
a Daoist priest,
courtesy name Jūnfáng,
later also attained the Way.
Yíngzhōu
Yíngzhōu lies in the great Eastern Sea,
spanning four thousand lǐ in area,
roughly opposite to Kuàijī Commandery,
seven hundred thousand lǐ from the western shore.
It produces divine mushrooms and immortal herbs,
and also has tall jade stones,
nearly a thousand zhàng high,
from which springs flow with a taste like wine,
named the Jade Nectar Spring,
drinking a few shēng of it intoxicates,
granting eternal life.
Many immortal families dwell on the isle,
their customs similar to those of Wúzhōng,
its mountains and rivers resembling those of the Central Plains.
Xuánzhōu
Xuánzhōu is in the Northern Sea,
in the direction of Xū-Hài,
spanning seven thousand two hundred lǐ in area,
three hundred sixty thousand lǐ from the southern shore.
There is the Xuándū,
governed by the Immortal Elder Zhēngōng.
It abounds with hills and mountains,
and also has winds.
The mountains are often windy,
with air resonating like thunder and lightning.
Facing the northwestern gate of heaven,
it hosts many Great Mysterious Immortal Officials,
each with distinct palaces.
Rich in metals, stones, and purple mushrooms,
it is also a place governed by the Three Heavens.
Yánzhōu
Yánzhōu is in the Southern Sea,
spanning two thousand lǐ in area,
ninety thousand lǐ from the northern shore.
Upon it lives the wind-born beast,
resembling a leopard,
blue in color,
as large as a wildcat.
Nets are set to catch it,
and cartloads of firewood are piled to burn it,
yet when the wood is consumed, the beast does not ignite,
standing in the ashes,
its fur unscorched.
It cannot be cut or pierced,
striking it feels like hitting a leather bag,
only by hammering its head thousands of times with an iron mallet can it be killed,
but if it opens its mouth towards the wind,
it revives in a short while.
Stuffing its nostrils with calamus from stones causes its death,
taking its brain and consuming it with yellow chrysanthemums,
after ten jīn,
grants a lifespan of five hundred years.
There is also the Fire Forest Mountain,
in which dwells the fire-light beast,
as large as a rat,
with fur three to four cùn long,
either red or white.
The mountain spans about three hundred lǐ,
on dark nights, this mountain forest is often seen,
illuminated by this beast's glow,
resembling firelight.
Taking its fur to weave into cloth,
people of the time call it 'fire-cleaning cloth'.
The inhabitants wear it as clothing,
if it becomes soiled,
washing it with ashes
never cleans it.
Only by burning it in fire for the time of two meals,
then shaking it,
does the dirt fall off on its own,
leaving it white as snow.
Many immortal families also reside here.
Chángzhōu
Chángzhōu,
also named Qīngqiū,
is in the Southern Sea in the direction of Chén-Sì.
Spanning five thousand lǐ in area,
it is two hundred thousand lǐ from the shore.
Rich in mountains and rivers,
and also abundant with large trees.
Some trees measure two thousand arm spans around.
Across the entire isle,
it is exclusively covered with forests,
hence the name Qīngqiū.
It possesses immortal herbs and divine medicines,
sweet dews and jade essences,
and also has the Wind Mountain,
which often rumbles.
There is the Zǐfǔ Palace,
where heavenly immortals and fairy maidens roam.
Yuánzhōu
Yuánzhōu is in the Northern Sea,
spanning three thousand lǐ in area,
one hundred thousand lǐ from the southern shore.
Upon it are the Five Mushrooms and the Mysterious Stream,
whose water is like honey nectar,
drinking it grants eternal life,
lasting as long as heaven and earth.
Consuming the Five Mushrooms,
also leads to immortality.
Many immortal families dwell here.
Liúzhōu
Liúzhōu is in the Western Sea,
spanning three thousand lǐ in area,
one hundred ninety thousand lǐ from the eastern shore.
It abounds with mountains, rivers, and accumulated stones,
named Kūnwú.
Smelting these stones into iron to make swords,
they shine brilliantly,
like crystal in appearance,
cutting jade as if it were mud.
Many immortal families also reside here.
Shēngzhōu
Shēngzhōu is in the Eastern Sea between Chǒu and Yín,
connecting to Pénglái seven hundred thousand lǐ away,
spanning two thousand five hundred lǐ in area,
two hundred thirty thousand lǐ from the western shore.
Tens of thousands of immortal families dwell here.
The climate is peaceful and harmonious,
with immortal herbs often growing and the land free from cold or heat,
nurturing all things.
It also has many mountains, rivers, immortal herbs, and various mushrooms.
The water throughout the isle
tastes like sweet syrup or cheese.
It is the most excellent of isles.
Fènglínzhōu
Fènglín (Phoenix and Unicorn),
is located in the Western Sea,
covering an area of fifteen hundred lǐ.
The continent is surrounded by weak water on all sides,
where even a swan's feather cannot float,
making it impassable.
On the continent, there are numerous phoenixes and unicorns, numbering in the tens of thousands,
each forming their own groups.
There are also mountains, rivers, ponds, marshes, and a hundred kinds of divine herbs,
as well as many immortal dwellings.
Boiling the beaks of phoenixes and the horns of unicorns together to make a glue,
it is named "Xùxián Jiāo" (Bowstring-Mending Glue),
or sometimes called "Liánjīn Ní" (Gold-Joining Paste).
This glue can mend broken bowstrings of crossbows,
and reconnect severed blades of swords and knives.
When the rejoined part is tested,
by having strong men pull it apart,
it breaks elsewhere,
while the mended section remains completely undamaged.
In the third year of the Tiānhàn era,
Emperor Wǔ journeyed to the Northern Sea to sacrifice at Héng Shān.
In the fourth month,
an envoy from the King of the Western Regions arrived,
presenting four liǎng of divine glue and a Jíguāng fur robe.
Emperor Wǔ accepted them and stored them in the outer treasury,
unaware of the marvelous properties of the glue and the robe.
He thought that although the Western Regions were distant,
their tribute was not extraordinary,
so he detained the envoy without sending him back.
Some time later, Emperor Wǔ visited the Huálín Garden,
and while shooting a tiger, his crossbow string snapped.
The envoy, who was accompanying the imperial carriage,
offered a portion of the glue,
and had someone moisten it with saliva to mend the bowstring.
The emperor exclaimed in amazement, "This is a rare object!"
He then ordered several warriors,
to pull it together from opposite sides,
but it held fast all day without coming apart,
as if it had never been broken.
The glue is green like jasper,
and the Jíguāng fur robe is yellow,
likely from a type of divine horse.
The robe does not get wet even after several days in water,
nor does it burn in fire.
The emperor then realized their value.
He richly rewarded the envoy and sent him on his way.
He also came to appreciate Dōngfāng Shuò's foresight even more.
During the time of King Mù of Zhōu,
the Western Hú presented a Kūnwú knife and a "Ever-Full Cup" that glowed at night.
The knife was one chǐ long,
and the cup could hold three shēng.
The knife could cut jade as if it were mud,
and the cup, made from the essence of white jade,
shone brightly through the night.
If placed in the courtyard facing the sky at dusk,
by dawn it would be filled with water,
sweet and fragrant to the taste,
truly a vessel of the spirits.
During Qín Shǐhuáng's reign,
the Western Hú presented a jade-cutting knife,
but there was no longer an Ever-Full Cup.
As for the origin of this glue,
it comes from the Fènglín Continent.
The swords originate from
the Liú Continent.
Both are found in the Western Sea.
Jùkū Continent
The Gathering Mound Continent lies in the western sea at the southwest location,
covering an area of three thousand li.
To the north, it connects with Kūnlún two hundred sixty thousand li away,
and is two hundred forty thousand li from the eastern shore.
It is home to many divine immortals and spiritual officials,
with palaces and residences lining the streets,
too numerous to count.
There are also lions, bìxié beasts, záochǐ monsters, tiānlù deer, and creatures with bronze heads and iron brows.
On the continent stands a great mountain,
shaped like a human-bird,
hence named the "Human-Bird Mountain."
It abounds with large trees,
similar to maple trees.
Their fragrant forests and leaves
can be smelled from hundreds of li away.
These are the "Soul-Returning Trees."
They can also produce sounds
like a herd of oxen roaring,
and those who hear it
are all shaken in heart and terrified in spirit.
Cutting their roots
and boiling the sap in a jade cauldron,
then simmering over low heat until it resembles black tin,
it can be formed into pills,
named "Startling Essence Incense,"
or called "Trembling Spirit Pills,"
or "Far-Born Incense,"
or "Quivering Sandalwood Incense,"
or "Human-Bird Essence,"
or "Death-Repelling Incense."
One substance with six names,
it is indeed a spiritual object.
Its fragrance can be smelled for hundreds of li.
The dead lying on the ground, upon smelling its aroma,
are revived,
never to perish again.
Using the incense to fumigate the deceased
yields even more miraculous effects.
After this,
in the third year of Yánhé,
Emperor Wǔ visited Āndìng.
The king of the Yuèzhī country of the Western Hú sent an envoy to present four liǎng of incense,
as large as sparrow eggs,
black as mulberries.
The emperor, considering it not native to the Middle Kingdom,
stored it in the outer treasury.
They also offered a fierce beast,
shaped like a fifty- or sixty-day-old puppy,
resembling a wildcat but yellow in color.
The envoy was ordered to present it.
The emperor saw the envoy holding it,
and due to its frail, thin, bald, and haggard appearance,
found it strange that such a tribute was offered.
He asked the envoy, "This creature seems playable;
how can it be called a fierce beast?"
The envoy replied, "That which imposes majesty upon all creatures
need not be judged by size.
Thus, the divine qílín is king to the giant elephant,
the luánphoenix is sovereign to the great péng bird,
and the centipede is subdued by the téng snake,
which also does not depend on size.
My country is three hundred thousand li from here,
and we have constant omens: when the east wind harmonizes with the pitch pipes,
blowing for a hundred days without cease,
and azure clouds align with the lǜ tones,
lingering for months unbroken,
we know the Middle Kingdom will have a ruler devoted to the Way.
My king thus scorns Confucians and Mohists but honors the Dào and its virtue,
despises gold and jade but treasures spiritual objects.
Therefore, we searched for rare treasures,
offered divine incense,
traversed celestial forests to seek the fierce beast,
rode felt-covered carts to cross weak abysses,
and spurred swift steeds to traverse flying sands.
We journeyed through distant paths,
enduring hardships on rugged roads until now,
for thirteen years.
The divine incense cures fatal diseases of demonic afflictions,
and the fierce beast repels all evil spirits and ghosts.
These two objects
are truly essential for nurturing life
and aiding governance to pacify the realm.
How could Your Majesty fail to recognize their authenticity?
This must be an error in our country's wind divination!
Today, upon beholding Your Majesty's countenance,
I see you are not a ruler devoted to the Way.
Eyes that gaze too much lead to lust;
mouths that speak too much invite trouble;
bodies that move too much incite turmoil;
hearts that adorn too much breed extravagance.
None who indulge in these four
can achieve order under heaven."
Emperor Wǔ, angered and unsettled,
asked the envoy further, "In what way does this fierce beast subdue all creatures?
What does it eat?
From where does its strength come?
And what land gives it birth?"
The envoy said, "The fierce beast originates
sometimes from Kūnlún,
sometimes from Xuánpǔ,
sometimes from the Gathering Mounds,
sometimes from Tiānlù.
Its lifespan is immeasurable,
it feeds on ether and drinks dew,
understands human speech,
and embodies benevolence, kindness, loyalty, and forgiveness—
such is its virtue;
it protects even the lowliest creatures,
never harming those below tigers and leopards—
such is its majesty;
with one cry unleashed,
thousands prostrate in silence,
oxen and horses tremble in fear,
tethers snap in alarm,
warriors falter suddenly,
losing all strength—
such is its divinity;
it raises wind and clouds at will,
spews and spits rain and dew,
drives all evils to flee,
and makes jiāo dragons and soaring serpents
dwell in the stables of Tàishān,
commanding lions in service—
thus it is named the fierce beast.
Its divine transformations are boundless,
able to be the sovereign of great birds,
the primal king under heaven's canopy,
the chief beast that wards off evil.
The spiritual incense, though small in quantity,
is a divine object of revival.
Those who die from plague or disaster
can be resurrected by it,
merely upon smelling its fragrance.
Its aroma is exceptionally potent,
hence hard to dissipate."
Thereupon, the emperor ordered the envoy to make the beast vocalize,
to test and hear it.
The envoy then pointed at the beast,
commanding it to utter one sound.
The beast licked its lips for a long while,
then suddenly cried out like a thunderclap in the sky,
while its eyes flashed with intersecting lights,
its vital energy soaring heavenward,
lasting a long time before ceasing.
The emperor immediately stumbled and fell,
covering his ears, shaken,
unable to control himself.
The guards and tiger-warriors
all dropped their weapons and prostrated on the ground,
while all oxen, horses, dogs, pigs, and such
broke free from their tethers,
running wild in terror,
calming only after a long while.
The emperor, wary of it,
sent the beast to the Shànglín Park,
ordering tigers to devour it.
But when the tigers heard it coming,
they gathered in their dens,
lying like dead tigers.
As the beast entered the park,
it径直 climbed onto a tiger's head and urinated into its mouth,
then retreated about ten steps away,
glanced back at the tiger,
and the tiger promptly closed its eyes.
The emperor resented the envoy's insolent words,
and intended to arrest him.
The next day,
both the envoy and the fierce beast had vanished.
Searches were sent out in all directions,
but their whereabouts remained unknown.
Later, in the first year of Hòuyuán Fēng,
when thousands fell ill in Cháng'ān city,
and more than half died,
they tried burning the Yuèzhī divine incense within the city.
All who had died within three days revived,
and the fragrance lingered for three months without fading.
Only then did they believe in its divine nature.
So, they secretly recorded the incense,
but one day it disappeared again,
the box and seal intact as before,
with no incense left.
The emperor later regretted not treating the envoy with respect,
and valued more the teachings left by Fāng Shuò.
He felt ashamed for not diligently seeking Shào Jūn's wisdom,
and embarrassed that Wèi Qīng had left again.
Had he treated the envoy generously,
there would surely have been benefits.
The above is the ten continents
Cāng Sea Island
The Cāng Sea lies within the Northern Sea,
spanning three thousand li in area,
with the sea encircling islands on all four sides,
each extending five thousand li.
Its waters are all azure in color,
which is why immortals call it the "Cāng Sea."
The islands are dominated by great mountains and accumulated stones,
featuring famous stone formations,
including eight types of stones: shínǎo, shíguìyīng, liúyuè, huángzǐ, shídǎn, and over a hundred others,
all growing on the islands,
and consuming them grants one immortality.
Beyond this, a circular sea surrounds the mountains,
with waters pitch black in color,
called the Míng Sea.
It has towering waves a hundred zhang high even without wind,
making it impossible to traverse.
Above reside the Nine Elders and the Nine Heavens True Lords,
likely the dwelling place of the Supreme True Immortals,
accessible only to flying immortals.
Kūnlún
is also known as Kūnlíng,
located in the xū sector of the Western Sea,
and the hài sector of the Northern Sea.
It spans ten thousand li in area,
and is 130,000 li from the shore.
It is encircled by the Ruò River,
with its southeast connecting to the Jīshí Garden,
its northwest to the Northern Door Chamber,
its northeast bordering the Great Vital Well,
and its southwest reaching the Chéngyuān Valley,
these four great mountains at the corners serving as supports to Kūnlún.
At the southern end of the Jīshí Garden is the Queen Mother's palace.
The Queen Mother informed King Mù of Zhōu:
"The mountain is 360,000 li from Xiányáng,
and rises 36,000 li above the flat land,
with three peaks atop,
each spanning ten thousand li in breadth,
shaped like an overturned basin,
narrow at the bottom and wide at the top,
hence called the Three Peaks of Kūnlún Mountain.
One peak faces the chén direction,
named Làngfēng Summit;
one peak faces due west,
named Xuánpǔ Hall;
one peak faces due east,
named Kūnlún Palace.
One peak has accumulated gold,
forming the Great Yōng City,
with a surface area of a thousand li square.
On the city stand five golden platforms
and twelve jade towers.
From the Northern Door Mountain and Chéngyuān Mountain, one enters the Yōng City,
where golden platforms and jade towers reflect each other,
like the Flowing Essence Gate,
the Radiant Jasper Hall,
and the Qiónghuā Chamber,
adorned with purple, emerald, cinnabar, and azure.
Scenic clouds illuminate the sun,
with crimson clouds and ninefold light,
this is where the Queen Mother of the West governs.
Beyond the Northern Sea lies Zhōng Mountain,
in the zǐ sector of the Northern Sea,
separated by 19,000 li north of the Ruò River,
standing 13,000 li high,
with a summit of seven thousand li across,
and a circumference of thirty thousand li.
It naturally grows a thousand types of glossy ganoderma and over forty divine herbs.
Above are golden platforms and jade gates,
also a dwelling of primordial qì,
where the Heavenly Emperor rules.
South of Zhōng Mountain is Píngxié Mountain,
north is Jiāolóng Mountain,
west is Zhìcǎo Mountain,
east is Shùmù Mountain.
These four mountains
are branches of Zhōng Mountain.
They tower 30,000 li above Zhōng Mountain,
with five palace cities.
If one ascends any of these four mountains,
looking down, one can see Zhōng Mountain.
These four mountains
form the emperor's domain.
They also serve as paths for immortals to come and go,
with one route entering a cave southeast from Píngxié Mountain,
leading to the Purple Stone Chamber Palace on the inner Longevity Island,
where the Nine Elders' Immortal Capital is governed,
with tens of thousands of immortal officials.
Recorded.
Fāngzhàng Isle
lies at the center of the Eastern Sea,
with southwestern and northeastern shores equal in length,
each side of Fāngzhàng measuring five thousand li.
It is exclusively where dragons gather.
There are palaces of gold, jade, and lapis lazuli,
governed by the Director of Destinies of the Three Heavens.
Immortals wishing to ascend to heaven
come and go to this isle,
receiving the Supreme Mysterious Life Register.
Tens of thousands of immortal households
cultivate fields of jade and glossy ganoderma herbs, measured in acres,
like planting rice.
There is also a Stone Spring Mountain,
where the Jiǔyuán Elder presides,
commanding all water deities, dragons, snakes, giant whales, shadowy spirits, and aquatic creatures.
Fúsāng
is ten thousand li east of the Eastern Sea's shore,
where one finds the Bì Sea.
Vast and boundless,
it matches the eastern shore in size,
with waters not salty or bitter but purely azure,
sweet and fragrant in taste.
Fúsāng lies within the Bì Sea,
spanning a hundred li in area,
where the Supreme Emperor and True King Father govern.
The land is rich in trees,
with leaves like mulberry,
and also bears mulberry fruit.
The tallest trees reach several thousand zhang in height,
with trunks over three thousand arm-spans around.
Trees grow in pairs from the same root,
leaning on each other,
hence the name Fúsāng (Supporting Mulberry).
Immortals who eat its fruit
turn entirely golden,
soaring through the mystic void.
Though the trees are large,
their leaves resemble those of mulberry trees in central Xià.
However, the fruit is rare and red,
bearing once every nine thousand years,
with an exceptionally sweet and fragrant taste.
The land produces purple gold and round jade,
as common as tiles and stones in various Xià regions.
Its immortal officials transform in myriad ways,
often without fixed form.
Some split into a hundred bodies, each ten zhang tall.
Péngqiū
is Pénglái Mountain.
Facing the northeastern shore of the Eastern Sea,
it has a circumference of five thousand li.
To the north, it reaches outside the Northern E Gate of Zhōng Mountain,
where the Heavenly Emperor oversees the fabric of the Nine Heavens,
of incomparable nobility.
The mountain's source encircles it,
featuring four cities,
with a high mountain at its center,
resembling Kūnlún.
In the past, after Yǔ controlled the floods,
he rode in a qiāo chariot,
crossed the Ruò River, and arrived here,
offering sacrifices to God at the Northern E,
attributing his great achievement to the Nine Heavens.
Yǔ also traversed the Five Peaks,
having artisans carve stones,
recording distances and elevations,
in tadpole script,
unintelligible to Hàn people.
The measurements and distances recorded today are from Yǔ's time,
not only inscribed on the Five Peaks
but on other famous mountains as well.
The places where they were carved are uniquely elevated.
From Dōngfāng Shuò's "Record of the Ten Continents and Three Islands."
In our dynasty,
the Ten Great Grotto-Heavens
are located among the famed mountains of the earth,
where heaven dispatches groups of immortals to govern.
From "The Cloudy Bookcase's Seven Slips: Chart of Celestial Palaces and Earthly Prefectures."
The first is Wángwū Mountain,
with its celestial peak supremely lofty,
summit 120 li high,
and a grotto circumference of ten thousand li,
named the "Minor Heaven of Clear Emptiness."
Governed by Dù Zhòng and Wáng Bāo as the Minor Heaven King and Clear Emptiness True Immortal,
it lies on the border between Luòyáng and Héjiān,
sixty li from Wángwū County.
The "Cloudy Bookcase" states:
"Governed by Lord Wáng of Xīchéng."
The second is Wěiyǔ Mountain Grotto,
with a circumference of ten thousand li,
named the "Great Heaven of Empty Light."
Governed by Sī Jì and Wáng as the Great True Immortal,
it is in Táizhōu's Huángyán County.
The "Cloudy Bookcase" states:
"Governed by the Pure Youth Lord."
The third is Xīchéng Mountain,
two thousand zhang high,
with a grotto circumference of three thousand li,
named the "Great Mystery Heaven of Total Truth."
Governed by the True Immortal Wáng Fāngpíng,
it is a thousand li west of Chéngdū Prefecture in Liángzhōu,
bordering the western frontier.
The "Cloudy Bookcase" states:
"Location unknown." The "Secret Instructions for Ascending to Perfection" suggests:
The fourth: Xīxuán Mountain,
standing 2,700 zhàng high,
with a cavern perimeter of 1,000 lǐ,
named "Heaven of the Three Mysteries and Ultimate Truth."
It is administered by Perfected Péi,
located in Huàzhōu bordering the Western Fan region.
The Yúnjí states:
"It is likely inaccessible by human footsteps."
The fifth: Qīngchéng (Great Face) Mountain,
3,600 zhàng high,
with a cavern perimeter of 2,000 lǐ,
named "Heaven of the Nine Chambers Preserving Immortals."
It is administered by Perfected Nìng,
where the Yellow Emperor sought the Way from Xīyí,
and the True Lord bestowed upon the Yellow Emperor the "Scripture of the Dragon's Traversal,"
in Qīngchéng County, Shǔzhōu.
The Yúnjí states:
"Administered by the Elder of Qīngchéng."
The sixth: Tiāntāi Chìchéng Mountain,
18,000 zhàng high,
with a cavern perimeter of 500 lǐ,
named "Heaven of Upper Clarity and Jade Peace."
It is administered by Perfected Lord Tóngbò,
where Immortal Elder Gě Xuán refined elixirs and attained the Way,
corresponding to the Tái constellation above,
hence named "Tiāntāi,"
in Tiāntāi County, Táizhōu.
The Yúnjí states:
"In Tángxīng County, Táizhōu,
administered by Immortal Elder Yǔ Xuánzhōu."
The seventh: Luófú Mountain,
3,600 zhàng high,
with a cavern perimeter of 500 lǐ,
named "Heaven of Vermilion Brightness Shining Truth."
It is an island of Pénglái.
During Yáo's time, it floated across the sea with the great flood,
moored at Luó Mountain,
the two mountains joined,
hence named "Luófú Mountain."
It is where Bàopǔzǐ, Master Gě, refined elixirs and attained the Way,
in Bóluó County, Huìzhōu.
The Yúnjí states:
"Administered by the Former King Qīngjīng."
The eighth: Máo Mountain,
1,700 zhàng high,
with a cavern perimeter of 1,500 lǐ,
named "Heaven of the Golden Altar and Huáyáng."
The cavern contains raw gold,
with an altar 100 zhàng high,
and purple jade palaces,
all realms where Perfected Ones of Upper Clarity roam and rest.
Formerly named "Jūqǔ Mountain,"
it was renamed "Máo Mountain" after Lord Máo refined elixirs and attained the Way there,
in Jūróng County, Shēngzhōu.
The Yúnjí states:
"Administered by Perfected Zǐyáng."
The ninth: Línwū Mountain,
with a cavern perimeter of 400 lǐ,
named "Heaven of the Left Spirit's Hidden Ruins."
Also called "Bāo Mountain,"
located in Lake Tàihú,
where after Yǔ the Great controlled the floods,
he hid the Numinous Treasure Five Treasuries in this cavern,
now at the mouth of Dòngtíng Lake, Sūzhōu.
The Yúnjí states:
"Administered by the Perfected of Northern Peak."
The tenth: Kuòcāng Mountain,
with a cavern perimeter of 300 lǐ,
named "Heaven of Accomplished Virtue and Hidden Truth."
It is administered by Perfected Xú Láiqín,
in Xiānjū County, Táizhōu.
The Yúnjí states:
"Called the Cavern of Accomplished Virtue and Hidden Mystery,
north of Lè'ān County, Chùzhōu,
administered by Hǎigōng Juānzǐ."
Above from Lǐ Sīcōng's "Collection of Cavern Abysses"
Thirty-Six Minor Cavern Heavens
Next are the thirty-six minor cavern heavens,
located among various famous mountains,
also places governed by superior immortals.
From the Yúnjí.
The first: Huòtóng Mountain,
3,400 zhàng high,
with a cavern perimeter of 3,000 lǐ,
named "Heaven of Huò Forest."
It is administered by Perfected Ones Zhèng Sīyuǎn, Hán Zhòng, and Xǔ Yìng as Lords of the Directorate of Destiny,
in Chángxī County, Fúzhōu.
The Yúnjí states:
"Administered by Immortal Wáng Wěixuán."
The second: Eastern Peak Tài Shān,
4,000 zhàng high,
with a cavern perimeter of 1,000 lǐ,
named "Heaven of Péngxuán Empty Grotto."
Tàihào serves as the Green Emperor,
governing the Eastern Peak, presiding over all things, and examining deceased souls and ghosts.
It is the peak where emperors throughout history conducted fēngshàn rituals to report achievements.
Above, it corresponds to the essence of Lóu and Kuí constellations,
below, it stabilizes the celestial division of the Lǔ region,
located in Fèngfú County, Yǎnzhōu.
The Yúnjí states:
"Qiánfēng County."
The third: Southern Peak Héng Shān,
4,000 zhàng high,
with a cavern perimeter of 2,000 lǐ,
named "Heaven of Vermilion Mausoleum and Great Void."
Shénnóng serves as the Red Emperor governing the Southern Peak.
In the past, the Supreme God bestowed jade tablets and a precious seal,
granting the True Lord of Life Annotation to eternally guard the numinous peak.
It is the mountain that matches our emperor's longevity.
Above, it corresponds to the essence of Yì and Zhěn constellations and the jade衡 instrument,
hence named "Héng Shān."
Below, it stabilizes the celestial division of the Chǔ region,
located in Héngshān County, Héngzhōu.
The fourth: Western Peak Huà Shān,
7,000 zhàng high,
with a cavern perimeter of 2,000 lǐ,

named "Heaven of the Great Ultimate and All Immortals," where Shàohào serves as the White Emperor governing the Western Peak. The giant spirit god split it above with his hand and cleaved it below with his feet to open the river's flow, saving people from the flood disaster. The shape of the immortal's palm shines brilliantly to the eye. Above, it corresponds to the essence of Jǐng and Guǐ constellations.
Below, it stabilizes the celestial division of the Qín region,
located in Huàyīn County, Huàzhōu.
The Yúnjí states:
"Administered by Zhèng Zǐzhēn."
The fifth: Northern Peak Héng Shān,
2,900 zhàng high,
with a cavern perimeter of 2,000 lǐ,
named "Heaven of the Great One and Comprehensive Mystery."
Zhuānxū serves as the Black Emperor governing the Northern Peak,
with five names: first, "Orchid Terrace Prefecture,"
second, "Palace of Exemplary Women,"
third, "Huáyáng Terrace,"
fourth, "Purple Tenuity Terrace,"
fifth, "Palace of the Great One."
Above, it corresponds to the essence of Bì and Mǎo constellations,
below, it stabilizes the celestial division of the Yān region,
presiding over the office of grain abundance and ripening,
located in Héngshān County, Dìngzhōu.
The sixth: Central Peak Sōng Shān,
with a cavern 7,000 zhàng high,
perimeter of 1,000 lǐ,
named "Heaven of the Supreme God's Directorate of Truth."
The Sacred Ancestor serves as the Yellow Emperor governing the Central Peak,
presiding over virtue and distributing essence, where Huáng-Lǎo resides.
Above, there is the immortal's Bodhi tree
and the jade maiden's brocade-weaving terrace.
There are stone marrow, jade rings,
jade figures, and golden statues.
Above, it corresponds to the essence of Liǔ and Xīng constellations,
below, it stabilizes the celestial division of the Zhōu region,
located in Dēngfēng County, Luòjīng.
The Yúnjí states:
"Administered by Immortal Dèng Yúnshān."
The seventh: Éméi Mountain,
with a cavern perimeter of 300 lǐ,
named "Heaven of Ethereal Numen and Supreme Wonder."
It is administered by the Perfected of the Jade Emperor,
where the Yellow Emperor once sought the Way from the Perfected,
who bestowed upon the Emperor the "Scripture of the Three Ones,"
still transmitted in the world.
Yán Jūnpíng assists in governing this mountain,
located in Éméi County, Jiāzhōu.
The Yúnjí states:
"Named 'Cavern Heaven of Ethereal Mound,'
administered by Perfected Táng Lǎn."
The eighth: Lú Mountain,
3,900 zhàng high,
with a cavern perimeter of 1,700 lǐ,
named "Heaven of Immortal Numen Chanting Truth."
Ancient name: "Three Peaks Mountain of the Son of Heaven."
During King Chéng of Zhōu's time,
there was Master Fāng Fǔ,
courtesy name Jūnxiào,
who rode a white donkey into the mountain,
built a thatched hut,
refined elixirs, and attained the Way,
hence named "Lú Mountain."
It is administered by Perfected Wáng and two others,
along with Zhào Shēng, in Jiāngzhōu.
The Yúnjí states:
"Named 'Cavern Numen,'
administered by Perfected Tàizhēn during Zhōu Zhèng's time."

The tenth, Yángmíng Shān,

It is the site where the Yu Cave stores books,

The Yúnjí records: "North of the Kuàijī Shān cave in Jìng Hú,
Immortal Guō Cǎo governs it."

with a shrine,
now in Cháng'ān.

Immortal Zhāng Jìlián governs it."
The twelfth, Xī Shān,

The Yúnjí records: "Perfected Táng Gōngchéng governs it."
The thirteenth, Dàwéi Shān,

The Yúnjí records: "Xiǎowéi Shān cave,
Immortal Huā Qiūlín governs it."

seven thousand zhàng high with a cave perimeter of three hundred lǐ,

This is where Perfected Zuǒ Cí refined elixirs and attained the Dao,
and where the Imperial Ancestor, the Nine Heavens Director of Destinies, administers,

The Yúnjí records: "Immortal Jì Qiūzǐ governs it."
The fifteenth, Guǐgǔ Shān,
with a cave perimeter of seventy lǐ,

It is where Perfected Zhèngyī, Celestial Master Zhāng, refined elixirs and attained the Dao,

The Yúnjí records: "Named 'Guì Xuán Managing Truth Heaven',
Perfected Cuī Wénzǐ governs it."
The sixteenth, Wǔyí Shān,
with a cave perimeter of one hundred and twenty lǐ,

governed by Lord Wǔyí,
in Chóng'ān County, Jiànzhōu.
The Yúnjí records: "Perfected Liú Shàogōng governs it."
The seventeenth, Wǎngsì Shān,
with a cave thirty lǐ high,
and a perimeter of one hundred and eighty lǐ,

Formerly known as "Peak of Assembled Jades."
In ancient times, Emperor Wu of Han built an altar to receive the Shàngqīng registers,

In the cave, there is the Valley of Lush Apricot Blossoms,
governed by the Supreme Elegance Heavenly King,

where the nine Han perfected, Dù Tányǒng and Xiāo Zǐyún, refined elixirs, attained the Dao, and ascended,
at the Flying Immortal Stone and Cultivating Simplicity Platform on Chìsōng Peak,
in Xīngàn County, Línjiāng Army.
The Yúnjí records: "Perfected Liáng Bóluán governs it."
The eighteenth, Huágài Shān,
with a cave perimeter of four hundred lǐ,
is named "The Heaven of Róngchéng's Great Jade."
In Yǒngjiā County, Wēnzhōu.
The Yúnjí records: "Immortal Liáng Gōngxiū governs it."
The nineteenth, Gàizhú Shān,
with a cave perimeter of one hundred and eighty lǐ,
is named "The Heaven of Long Radiance and Precious Primordiality."
It is where Emperor Yŭ pacified this mountain,
and where Perfected Gé Xuán governed,
and where Master Bù attained the Dao,
in Huángyán County, Tāizhōu.
The Yúnjí records: "Immigrant Shāng Qiūzǐ governs it."
The twentieth, Dūqiáo Shān,
with a cave perimeter of one hundred and eighty lǐ,
is named "The Heaven of Precious Mystery."
In Pǔníng County, Róngzhōu.
The Yúnjí records: "Immigrant Liú Gēn governs it."
The twenty-first, Báishí Shān,
with a cave perimeter of seven hundred lǐ,
is named "The Heaven of Jade Elegance and Long Truth."
In Róngzhōu.
The Yúnjí records: "In Hánshān County, Hézhōu,
Perfected Bái governs it."
The twenty-second, Gōulòu Shān,
with a cave perimeter of three hundred lǐ,
is named "The Heaven of Jade Pass and Precious Cassia."
It is where Perfected Gé refined white cinnabar,
in Běiliú County, Róngzhōu.
The Yúnjí records: "Immigrant Qián governs it."
The twenty-third, Jiǔyí Shān,
with a cave perimeter of three thousand lǐ,
is named "The Heaven of Facing Truth and Great Emptiness."
The sixty-ninth Confucius,
administered by the Supreme Perfected Duke of the Great Ultimate,
it is the residence of Perfected Hé Hóu,
where Shùn met and ascended with the golden elixir,
in Yánqìng County, Dàozhōu.
The Yúnjí records: "Immigrant Yán Zhēnqīng governs it."
The twenty-fourth, Dòngyáng Shān,
with a cave perimeter of one hundred and fifty lǐ,
is named "The Heaven of Hidden Observation in the Yang Cave."
In Chángshā County, Tánzhōu.
The Yúnjí records: "Perfected Liŭ governs it."
The twenty-fifth, Mùfù Shān,
with a cave perimeter of one hundred lǐ,
is named "The Heaven of Cave Truth and Great Mystery."
In Píngkāng County, Yuèzhōu.
The Yúnjí records: "In Yuèzhōu, Perfected Chén governs it."
The twenty-sixth, Dàyǒu Shān,
with a cave perimeter of one hundred lǐ,
is named "The Heaven of Great You's Splendid Mystery."
It is the residence of Master Shànjuǎn from Yao's time,
and where Zhāng Guǒ cultivated the Dao in the Tang dynasty,
in Yuánlíng County, Chénzhōu.
The Yúnjí records:
"Perfected Yǐn governs it."
The twenty-seventh, Jīntíng Shān,
with a cave perimeter of three hundred lǐ,
is named "The Heaven of Golden Court's Lofty Mystery."
In Shàn County, Yuèzhōu.
The Yúnjí records: "Immortal Elder Zhào governs it."
The twenty-eighth, Mágū Shān,
with a cave perimeter of one hundred and fifty lǐ,
is named "The Heaven of Cinnabar Clouds."
It is where the Southern Pole's Perfected Wáng Fāngpíng met Mágū here,
and the residence and ascension site of Cài Jīng,
in Nánchéng County, Jiànchāng Army.
The Yúnjí records: "Perfected Wáng governs it."
The twenty-ninth, Xiāndū Shān,
with a cave perimeter of three hundred lǐ,
is named "The Heaven of Mysterious Capital Praying for Immortals."
It is where the Yellow Emperor ascended riding a fire dragon,
in Jìnyún County, Chùzhōu.
The thirtieth, Qīngtián Shān,
with a cave perimeter of five hundred lǐ,
is named "The Heaven of Green Field's Great Crane."
It is where the Green Ox Taoist attained the Dao,
in Qīngtián County, Chùzhōu.
The Yúnjí records: "Perfected Fù governs it."
The thirty-first, Zhōng Shān,
with a cave perimeter of one hundred lǐ,
is named "The Heaven of Vermilion Lake and Great Life."
It is administered by Master Mǎ Míng,
in Shàngyuán County, Shēngzhōu.
The Yúnjí records: "Perfected Gōng governs it."
The thirty-second, Liángcháng Shān,
with a cave perimeter of thirty lǐ,
is named "The Heaven of Releasing Fate at Liangchang."
In Jùróng County, Rùnzhōu.
The Yúnjí records: "Perfected Lǐ governs it."
The thirty-third, Zǐgài Shān,
with a cave perimeter of eighty lǐ,
is named "The Heaven of Purple Mystery Illuminating the Cave."
In Yúháng County, Hángzhōu.
The Yúnjí records:
"In Chángyáng County, Jīngzhōu,
Perfected Shǔ Gōngyǔ governs it."
The thirty-fourth, Tiānmù Shān,
the mountain has two eyes,
the left eye three thousand zhàng high,
the right eye two thousand five hundred zhàng high,
with a cave perimeter of one hundred lǐ,
is named "The Heaven of Great Tenuity and Mysterious Canopy."
In Hángzhōu.
The thirty-fifth, Táoyuán Shān,
with a cave perimeter of seventy lǐ,

During the Qin dynasty, over a thousand people entered the cave to escape calamity,
and never came out,

It is where Perfected Huángpíng Qú refined elixirs and ascended.
In Wǔlíng County, Dǐngzhōu.
The Yúnjí records:
"Perfected Xiè governs it."
The thirty-sixth: Jīnhuá Mountain,
standing a thousand zhang high,
with a cave perimeter of five hundred li,
named "The Heaven of Jīnhuá Cave's Origin."
This is where Perfected Person Huáng Chūpíng encountered Chìsōngzǐ, commanded stones to become sheep, and attained the Dao,
located in Jīnhuá County, Wù Prefecture.
It corresponds to the Wù Star above,
hence named "Jīnhuá Mountain."
As the Yúnjí records:
"Governed by Perfected Person Dài."
From Lǐ Sīcōng's "Collection of Cavern Abysses."
Seventy-Two Blessed Lands
Next are the seventy-two blessed lands,
situated among great territories and famous mountains,
where the Supreme Deity commands Perfected Persons to govern them,
many being places where the Dao is attained.
From the Yúnjí.
First: Dìfèi Mountain.
Within the boundaries of Jūróng County, Jiāngníng Prefecture,
all are places where Táo Yǐnjū lived in seclusion,
governed by Perfected Person Xiè Yǔn.
Second: Gàizhú Mountain.
In Xiāndū County, Qú Prefecture,
governed by Perfected Person Shī Cún.
Third: Xiānkǎn Mountain.
Fifteen li from Liángchéng County, Wēn Prefecture,
near Báixī Grass Market,
governed by Perfected Person Zhāng Zhònghuá.
Fourth: Dōngxiānyuán.
In Huángyán County, Tāi Prefecture,
governed by Earth Immortal Liú Fènglín.
Fifth: Xīxiānyuán.
In Huángyán County, Tāi Prefecture,
on Qiáo Ridge, one hundred twenty li,
governed by Earth Immortal Zhāng Zhàoqī.
Sixth: Nántián Mountain.
East of the Eastern Sea,
accessible by boat travel,
governed by Perfected Person Liú.
Seventh: Yùliū Mountain.
Near Pénglái Island in the Eastern Sea,
inhabited by many true immortals,
governed by Earth Immortal Xǔ Mài.
Eighth: Qīngyǔ Mountain.
West of the Eastern Sea,
connecting with Fúsāng,
governed by Perfected Person Liú Zǐguāng.
Ninth: Yùmù Cave.
South of Yùsì Mountain,
this is the hermitage of Vice Minister Xiāo Zǐyún.
To this day, during overcast rains,
one can still hear the sounds of strings and flutes,
often encountered by woodcutters.
Presided over by Earth Immortal Chì Lǔbān.
Tenth: Dānxiá Cave.
On Mágū Mountain,
where Perfected Person Cài Jīng attained the Dao,
to this day, on rainy nights, bell and chime sounds are often heard.
Governed by Perfected Person Cài.
Eleventh: Jūn Mountain.
In the Dòngtíng-Qīngcǎo Lake,
governed by Earth Immortal Hóu Shēng.
Twelfth: Dàruò Cliff.
In Yǒngjiā County, Wēn Prefecture, east one hundred twenty li,
governed by Earth Immortal Lǐ Fānghuí.
Thirteenth: Jiāo Source.
North of Jiànyáng County, Jiàn Prefecture,
this is the hermitage of Perfected Person Yǐn.
Fourteenth: Língxū.
North of Tángxīng County, Tāi Prefecture,
this is where Mr. Báiyún lived in seclusion.
Fifteenth: Wò Prefecture.
South of Shàn County, Yuè Prefecture,
governed by Perfected Person Fāng Míng.
Sixteenth: Mǔ Ridge.
South of Shàn County, Yuè Prefecture,
governed by Perfected Person Wèi Xiǎn.
Seventeenth: Ruòyē Stream.

Pénglái Pot, Làngyuàn Garden, and the Five Numinous Mountains of the Seas
Guǎngchéng Mountain
is the Eastern Peak of Heaven.
Located within the Eastern Sea,
it is the foremost of the Five Peaks where life originates.
Upon it are jade-green mist towers,
jade trees and frosty woods,
purple sparrows and kingfisher phoenixes,
green lotus roots and white tangerines,
indescribable in form.
It is where the Celestial Lord of the Green Emperor, Língwēi,
commands myriad immortal officials, soldiers, and clerks to guard this mountain.
It governs the essence of the Year Star,
residing within the nine qi of the blue heaven.
Chánglí Mountain
is the Southern Peak of Heaven.
Located within the Southern Sea,
upon it are vermilion palaces and crimson towers,
red chambers and cinnabar rooms,
scarlet grass and red ganoderma,
rosy ointments and golden nectar,
indescribable in form.
All newly attained immortals under heaven
come to this palace,
to refine their forms and cleanse their substances,
harmonize yin and temper yang,
for the sake of longevity.
Gazing upon it long,
the Way is the Red Emperor, Celestial Lord, Chì Biāonù,
commanding myriad immortal officials and divine clerks to guard this mountain.
It governs the essence of the Sparkling Deluder,
residing within the two qi
of the cinnabar heaven.
Lìnéng Mountain
is the Western Peak of Heaven,
located within the Western Sea,
upon it are white flower towers,
the city of three primes,
the palace of jade springs,
jade forests and auspicious beasts,
indescribable in form.
It is the White Emperor, Celestial Lord, Bái Zhāojù,
commanding immortal officials
and divine clerks to guard this mountain.
It governs the essence of the Great White,
residing within the seven qi of the plain heaven.
Guǎngyě Mountain
is the Northern Peak of Heaven,
located within the Weak Water of the Northern Sea,
shaped like Kūnlún,
together with Fēngdū and Luó Mountain as the masters of yin energy,
upon it are many jade towers and precious towers,
golden elixirs and dragon ganoderma,
indescribable in form.
It is the Black Emperor, Celestial Lord, Yè Guāngjì,
commanding immortal officials and divine clerks to guard this mountain.
It governs the essence of the Chronographic Star,
residing within the five qi of the mysterious heaven.
Kūnlún Mountain
is the Central Peak of Heaven,
located between the eight seas,
aligned with the heart of heaven above,
shaped like an inverted cover,
broad at the top and narrow at the bottom,
rising in three tiers,
reaching the height of heaven, where the sun and moon
and the yellow and red paths intersect upon it,
and the three lights traverse.
To the east is called "Kūnlún,"
to the west "Xuánpǔ,"
to the north "Làngyuàn,"
to the south "Jīshí Mountain," "Great Cliff Mountain," "Water Spring Mountain," "Northern Door Mountain,"
each side ten thousand li in extent.
Upon it are towers of jade flowers,
halls of light and jade,
jade ponds and emerald waters,
where the Queen Mother of the West commands the multitude of immortals to reside.
The four peaks in the seas are its branches,
the ten continents and four islands enter the sea,
great rivers encircle its sides,
and at the summit's peak
are five golden platforms,
twelve jade towers,
a golden city a thousand li wide,
where the earth grows trees with golden roots,
forests of jade branches,
purple sparrows and kingfisher phoenixes,
green peaches and white plums,
a hundred treasures wondrous and solemn,
indescribable in detail.
It is the Yellow Emperor, Celestial Lord, Hán Shūniǔ,
commanding the great sage multitude of heaven to guard this mountain.
All are connected to the famous mountains of the Five Peaks,
with constant comings and goings of immortals,
examining the registers of life.
It governs the essence of the Quelling Star,
residing within the central origin, the one qi of heaven.
These five peaks beyond the seas
are the five guardians of heaven and earth,
the Five Peaks of creation,
the ancestral source of the five qi.

History
Wáng Qiáo possessed divine arts,
served as magistrate of Yè County,
and on the last and first days of each month,
would travel from the county to the court for audiences.
The emperor suspected him of deceiving people with illusions.
Also in Hénán, there was Qū Shèngqīng,
skilled at creating talismans with red and black ink,
who subdued ghosts and spirits and commanded them.
There was also Biān Máng,
who likewise communicated with ghosts and spirits.
"Biography of Xiè Núgū".
Mèng Jié could hold a date pit in his mouth without eating,

He could also hold his breath without breathing,

"Biography of Wáng Zhēn".
Zhāng Kǎi had a natural inclination for Daoist arts,

"Original Biography".

"Original Biography in the Book of Jin".
Fán Chángbīn of Shùnyáng was the magistrate of Jiànchāng,
and mobilized the people to build official ships in the Jiànchéng Mountains.
The officials ordered each person to make a pair of chopsticks,
Xìng Líng made his but had not submitted them,
and someone stole them.
Soon after, the thief felt heartache as if dying,
Líng said to him: "Did you perhaps steal my chopsticks?"
The thief did not respond.
After a while,
it worsened,
Líng said: "If you don't confess truthfully,
you will truly die now."
The thief became very anxious,
and confessed, producing them.
Líng then gave him water to drink,
and the illness was immediately cured.
From then on, people feared and respected him.
When the ship was completed,
and ready to launch,
the officials used two hundred people to pull one ship,
but it wouldn't move,
just as they were about to request more men,
Líng said: "This is already more than enough,
but the coordination is lacking.
I request to pull it myself."
Then, holding the chopsticks,
using only a hundred people,
the ship moved as if flowing.
The crowd was greatly astonished,
all proclaiming his divinity.
"Original Biography".

Biographies
Fèi Chángfáng encountered Hú Gōng, who possessed divine arts,
able to contract the earth's veins over a thousand miles,
gathering them before one's eyes,
and releasing them back to their original state.
From Gé Hóng's "Biographies of Immortals."
Later, in the Eastern Hàn, Luán Bā
was summoned by the Hàn emperor to serve as Shàngshū.
During the grand assembly at the court,
Bā arrived last,
appearing quite intoxicated,
yet instead of drinking, he sprayed wine toward the southwest.
Officials reported Bā for great disrespect.
The emperor inquired of Bā,
who replied: "My hometown, believing I could control ghosts and protect against illness,
built a temple for me.
This morning,
the elders all entered the temple to offer sacrifices,
hence my delay.
My home county Chéngdū caught fire,
so I sprayed wine to create rain and extinguish the flames."
The emperor pardoned his offense,
and immediately sent an envoy to verify his words.
The reply stated: "There was a fire on New Year's Day,
and during mealtime, heavy rain came from the northeast,
quenching it,
with the rain all carrying the scent of wine."
Later, one day, a great wind arose,
the sky grew foggy and dark,
and Bā disappeared.
Upon inquiry,
it was said that he returned to Chéngdū that day,
bid farewell to his relatives, and ascended to heaven.
Zuǒ Cí pulled out a hairpin and drew with it,
whereupon a cup of wine split in half,

Zuǒ Cí understood the Liù Jiǎ,

Liǔ Zhèng possessed Daoist arts.

Liú Gāng possessed Daoist arts,

Once, he competed in skills with his wife, Fán Fūrén.
Both seated in the hall,
Gāng created a fire to burn the mortar house,
starting from the east;
his wife restrained it,
and the fire extinguished immediately.
In the courtyard were two peach trees;
each chanted over one,
making them fight each other.
After a long while,
the one Gāng chanted over lost,
repeatedly fleeing outside the fence.
Gāng spat into a plate,
turning it into a carp.
His wife spat into a plate, creating an otter,
which ate the fish.
When Gāng and his wife entered Sìmíng Mountain,
a tiger blocked the path;
Gāng restrained it,
and the tiger crouched, not daring to move.
Just as he tried to pass,
the tiger roared at him.
His wife walked straight forward,
and the tiger turned its face to the ground,
not daring to look up.
She tied it with a rope, led it back, and tethered it to the bedpost.
When about to ascend to heaven,
Gāng, serving as magistrate of Shàngyú,
had a large皂荚 tree by the county office.
Gāng climbed the tree several zhàng high
before he could fly up.
His wife sat calmly,
rising gradually like mist,
and together they ascended to heaven.
From "Records of Female Immortals."

If the form resembles a living person,
it is shìjiě;
if the feet are not blue,
and the skin not wrinkled,
it is shìjiě;
if the gaze does not fade,
no different from a living person,
it is shìjiě;
if the hair falls out and the form and bones are lost,
it is shìjiě.
Some die and revive,

some leave clothes behind with the form gone,
some lose hair while the form flies away,

Liberation at daytime is superior,

Bào Jìng, governor of Nánhǎi,

Jìng said: "It's Jī Shūyè."
Níng said: "Jī faced execution at the eastern market;
how can he be here?"
Jìng replied: "Though Shūyè appeared to die,
he actually achieved shìjiě."
